title: Jump-Start Back-to-school Learning With Bank Of America Museums On Us
location: Multiple locations in New Jersey and NYC
description:
WHAT: Bank of America, Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank cardholders can receive FREE general admission to cultural attractions across New York City and New Jersey on Saturday and Sunday. 
WHEN: Saturday, September 5th & Sunday, September 6th (+ the first full weekend of each month) 
WHERE: Learn something new this month with a visit to a participating cultural institution, including:
Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum, 2 East 91st Street, New York, NY 10128
The Intrepid Museum, Pier 86 W 46th, New York, NY 10036
The Jewish Museum, 1109 5th Ave, New York, NY 10128 (Sundays only)
The Metropolitan Museum of Art – The Met Cloisters, 99 Margaret Corbin Dr, New York, NY 10040
The Metropolitan Museum of Art – The Met Fifth Avenue, 1000 5th Ave, New York, NY 10028
Hunterdon Art Museum, 7 Lower Center Street, Clinton, NJ 08809
Liberty Science Center, 222 Jersey City Boulevard, Jersey City, NJ 07305
Montclair Art Museum, 3 South Mountain Ave., Montclair, NJ 07042
Morris Museum, 6 Normandy Heights Road, Morristown, NJ 07960
The Newark Museum of Art, 49 Washington Street, Newark, NJ 07102
New York Botanical Garden, 2900 Southern Blvd., Bronx, NY 10458 
WHY: Bank of America believes the arts have a unique ability to connect people and communities and help local economies thrive. Through Museums on Us, Bank of America provides its cardholders with free access during the first full weekend of every month to artistic and cultural experiences in New Jersey at celebrated institutions ranging from art, children’s and history museums to botanical gardens, and science centers. This is one example of how the bank strengthens the local communities it serves in, creates greater cultural understanding, and expands accessibility to the arts. 
HOW: Use the bank’s location finder tool to search for participating cultural attractions. Please check with our partners directly for current operating hours and admission guidelines. Present your Bank of America, Merrill or Bank of America Private Bank credit or debit card along with a photo ID to gain free general admission to any participating institution during the first full weekend (Saturday and Sunday) of each month. Cardholders only; guests are not eligible for free admission. Program excludes fundraising events, special exhibitions, and ticketed shows. Not to be combined with other offers. Museum participation varies.

title: Verona Park
description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US FOR A WALK

We will meet at the benches in front of the boathouse.

We will walk the loop around the park. The goal will be at least three miles, but there is plenty of opportunity to stop or continue to fit your personal goals.

We will be walking on a paved surface.

We walk at a medium speed.

Please plan to arrive 5 minutes **early** so that we can **start on time.**

Verona Park is 54.32 acres with a lake running through it. It is bordered by Lakeside and Bloomfield Avenues in the southern part of Verona. It is the fifth largest park in the Essex County system, making it a great place to walk.

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap. Event will be canceled in the event of extreme weather.

title: NJ Singles Day Trip to NYC: Soulmate Photobooth, Dancing & Village Stroll
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
**One train ride. A whole day in the city. And you don't have to bring anyone.**
This is a **singles day trip from New Jersey into New York City** on the Saturday of Labor Day weekend. We meet at Newark Penn Station, ride in together, and spend the day doing three genuinely fun things with a group of people who all showed up for the same reason: to meet someone in real life instead of on an app.
No icebreaker circles. No name tags. No one making you introduce yourself to the room. Just a good day out where meeting people happens naturally.
\*\*\*
**☕ 10:00 AM — Meet at Newark Penn Station** Main concourse, by the NJ Transit departure board. I'll be posting what I will be wearing on the day before — look for me. Come at 9:50 if you're nervous; I'll be there early and we'll talk before anyone else shows up. *We leave at 10:20 sharp. Please be on time — we can't hold the group.*
**🚆 10:20 AM — Into the city together** **\- Transit to New York Penn Station\, about 20 minutes\,** Buy your ticket before you get there so we're not all in line at once. We ride together, which means the awkward part is over before we even arrive.
**📸 11:00 AM — The Soulmate Photobooth** **The Missed Connections Booth — outside Santo Taco, 94 University Place at E 12th St, Union Square, Manhattan.** You scan a QR code, answer a short compatibility quiz, and step into the booth. It prints two strips: one of you, and one of the stranger the algorithm picked as your match. **$10.** It's the best icebreaker in New York. By the time we walk away, everyone's comparing strips and laughing, and nobody's a stranger anymore.
**🌮 12:30 PM — Lunch around Union Square** Santo Taco is right there, and there's everything else within two blocks — sit-down, quick, veggie, whatever you're in the mood for. **We can stop by whenever. This is just tentative.**
**🚶🏽‍♀️ 2:00 PM — Stroll through Greenwich Village** Down through **Washington Square Park**, then into the **West Village** — the brownstones, the little streets, the sidewalk musicians. Easy pace, lots of stopping, lots of talking. This is the part where the real conversations happen. About 2 miles total, all flat, and we stop whenever people want to.
**💃🏽 5:00 PM — Dancing**\- TBA\. **No partner needed. No experience needed.** If you haven't danced in fifteen years, you're in good company — half of us haven't either. Come for one song and stay for six.
**🌙 8:00 PM — Head home, or stay out** We'll walk back toward the train together around 8. Stay later if the night's going well — you're a grown adult, nobody's checking.
\*\*\*
**Who this is for** Single adults **21 and over** who want to meet people face to face. Our crowd is a real mix, and it usually lands around 25+.The vibe is grown, warm, and easygoing — good conversation and good music, not a college bar night.
**Come alone.** Almost everyone does. That's the entire point.
**What it costs** Free to RSVP. You cover your own day:
No hidden fees, nothing collected up front, no upsell.
**Good to know**

* We're walking about 2–3 miles across the day, all flat. Wear shoes you'd walk a city in.
* **Bring Cash**
* There's alcohol at the dance venue, and **absolutely no pressure to drink**. Plenty of us won't be.
* Rain or shine. If the weather turns, the stroll becomes a longer lunch and we go dance early.
* Bring a portable charger. You'll take more photos than you think.

**Important Policies**
**Weather & Rain Date Policy:** This event may be postponed or rescheduled due to rain, severe weather, unsafe conditions, or circumstances beyond the organizers’ control. If the event is postponed, all tickets will automatically transfer to the announced rain date or rescheduled date. Refunds will not be issued if a ticket holder is unable to attend the new date. If the event is canceled by the organizers and no replacement date is scheduled, attendees will be contacted regarding available options.
**Liability and Assumption of Risk:** Participation is voluntary. Neither Yes We Thryve, NJ Singles, Catholic Singles NJ, nor their organizers, volunteers, instructors, venues, or hosts shall be responsible for any injury, illness, loss, theft, or property damage occurring during or in connection with the event, to the fullest extent permitted by law.
**Photography and Consent:** Photos and videos may be taken during the event for marketing, promotional, and community purposes. By attending, you consent to the use of your image in future promotions. Please notify an organizer at the event if you prefer not to be photographed or recorded.
**Email Subscription:** By RSVPing, you agree to be added to the Yes We Thryve and NJ Singles email lists for event announcements and community updates. You may unsubscribe at any time.
**Respect and Courtesy:** Please be kind and respectful toward venue staff, organizers, volunteers, and fellow guests. Disruptive, threatening, discriminatory, or inappropriate behavior may result in removal from the event without a refund.
**Arrival and Departure:** You are welcome to arrive late or leave early unless the event description states otherwise. This is intended to be a friendly, inclusive, and low-pressure environment where guests can connect in person.
**Ticket Policy:** All sales are final. Tickets are nonrefundable and non-transferable, except where otherwise stated by the organizers.

title: Is Your Marketing Built for Your Current Stage of Growth?
description:
Montclair Business Networking
What worked when your business was smaller may be slowing your growth now.
Growth requires change, but many companies don’t evolve their marketing strategy quickly enough.
The systems, team structure, processes, and investments that made sense at one stage can create inefficiency, inconsistent lead flow, or missed opportunities at the next stage.
So, how do you know if your marketing is where it should be?
On September 8 at 12 PM ET, join us for a virtual discussion on how marketing, sales, and operational strategies should evolve as businesses grow, and what companies at each stage should be doing differently.
What You’ll Learn

* Which marketing systems, automation tools, and infrastructure make sense at different stages of growth
* When to hire internally, outsource strategically, or keep marketing lean based on your company’s size, complexity, and growth goals
* What processes growing companies typically need to formalize to create more consistency and scalability
* How to strengthen lead generation, follow-up, sales alignment, and execution as your business becomes more complex
* The common mistakes companies make when their marketing doesn’t evolve with their growth

Who Should Attend

* Business owners and executives questioning whether their current marketing approach can support the next stage of growth
* Sales, marketing, and operations leaders responsible for driving revenue and efficiency
* Companies building, restructuring, or scaling
* Organizations looking to create more predictable growth without unnecessary overhead
source: Montclair Business Networking, Montclair Local News

title: Everything Book Club, "Kin" by Tayari Jones
location: Montclair Main - Tower Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
An instant New York Times bestseller by the author of "An American Marriage." A selection for both Oprah's Book Club and The New York Times Book Review Book Club. 

Goes with the Open Book / Open Mind program with Tayari Jones about "Kin" the following week on Tuesday, September 15! Tickets cost $35 and include a signed copy of the book. (If for any reason you can't afford a ticket, come talk to me.)

We'll talk about Jones's conversation as well as "Kin," a poignant historical novel set in the civil rights era about two motherless childhood friends who take very different journeys: one to the storied HBCU Spellman College, the other to make her way in the world. 

TAYARI JONES is the author of four others novels, most recently the New York Times bestseller "An American Marriage," which was an Oprah’s Book Club selection and also appeared on Barack Obama’s summer reading list and his year-end roundup. It won the Women’s Prize for Fiction, the Aspen Words Literary Prize, and an NAACP Image Award and has been published in two dozen countries. Jones is the C.H. Candler Professor of English and Creative Writing at Emory University and lives in Atlanta.

title: Library Speakers Consortium - Writing the Nightmare: A Ship Called Sickness and One Unforgettable Space Crew with Daniel Kraus
description:
You must register here to attend:  https://libraryc.org/nutleypubliclibrary/194581

Prepare to launch into the darkest depths of deep space! Join us as we sit down with master storyteller Daniel Kraus, winner of the 2026 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction, to celebrate the release of his breathtaking new novel, The Sixth Nik.

Deep into space, far past the triworld outposts, beyond range of the lethal trollbot internet, soars The Sickness: a ship woven from biomatter and capable of reacting to every need of its human crew. Sisilla, a nine-year-old cultist with a brain enhanced by arcane tech known as “niks,” has boarded to investigate the enigma of Fém—a plague-riddled planet that has abruptly gone rogue.

The mysterious crew includes a faceless assassin, a beautiful engineer jigsawed by plastic surgery, a peyote-addicted medic, and—most lethal of all—a rugged, NonModded captain with a score to settle with Sisilla. Other dangers abound. A hacked robot begins to believe Sisilla is its daughter. The Sickness itself is mutating, possibly even pregnant. And the secret of Fém is more horrific than anyone could have imagined. To survive, Sisilla will need to forsake her predetermined fate and embrace the unknown.

Register now to gain exclusive insight from one of the most visionary voices in modern fiction.

About the Author:

Daniel Kraus is a Pulitzer Prize-winning, New York Times bestselling writer of novels, TV, and film. His novel Angel Down was the 2026 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction winner, a New York Times Top 10 Book of 2025, and a national bestseller. His novel Whalefall received a front-cover review in the New York Times Book Review, won the Alex Award, was an L.A. Times Book Prize Finalist, and was a Best Book of 2023 from NPR, the New York Times, Amazon, Chicago Tribune, and more.

With Guillermo del Toro, he co-authored The Shape of Water, based on the same idea the two created for the Oscar-winning film. Also with del Toro, Kraus co-authored Trollhunters, which was adapted into the Emmy-winning Netflix series. He co-wrote The Living Dead and Pay the Piper with legendary filmmaker George A. Romero. Kraus’s The Death and Life of Zebulon Finch was named one of Entertainment Weekly‘s Top 10 Books of the Year. Kraus has won the Bram Stoker Award, Scribe Award, two Odyssey Awards (for both Rotters and Scowler), and has appeared multiple times as Library Guild selections, and more.

Kraus’s work has been translated into over 25 languages. He lives with his partner in Chicago. Visit him at danielkraus.com

title: Tuesday Night Figure Drawing - Open Studio
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Tuesday Night Figure Drawing – Open Studio 
*Cover art by Ling Chen. 











Tuesday night at The Space is your invitation to drop in, find your creative flow, and practice your drawing skills. 
Each week a different nude model serves as our muse as we pursue creative expression through observation and mark making. We challenge how we see and what we want to say — observing the nuances of the human form, its moods, character, and light — and do our best to capture something in the moment that tells a story. 
This has become a tight-knit, supportive community of seekers — artists, experimenters, and curious souls drawn together by the shared pursuit of capturing the living human form. Use the time to refine your skills, experiment with different media, and deepen your understanding of anatomy, gesture, and proportion. Challenge your process if you have one, or begin to develop one if you don’t. Learn to truly see. 
Each session features a variety of poses, from quick gesture sketches to longer, more detailed studies. Whether you’re looking to sharpen your technical abilities, loosen up your line work, or simply enjoy the meditative experience of drawing from life, this open studio is designed to support individual growth in a collaborative atmosphere. All skill levels are welcome – we’ve even had poets drop in and compose verses to the vibe in the room. 
Bring your preferred supplies — charcoal, graphite, ink, pastels, and paint are all welcome. Basic drawing materials are available if you don’t have any, and the shop has drawing pads and supplies for sale. No formal instruction is provided, but peer feedback and self-guided exploration are always part of the mix. 
Good music. Good people. See you Tuesday. 7 – 9:30 pm at the Space. 
Tickets are set at a capacity of 12, but we accommodate up to 18 for those paying in cash. 











“The object isn’t to make art, its to be in that wonderful state which makes art inevitable.” – Robert Henri

title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes)
description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

title: Finding Paddy
location: The Clairidge, 486 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, 07042, United States
description:
Montclair filmmaker Steve McCarthy looks at the life of his friend FDNY Captain Patrick “Paddy” Brown, after he dies in the World Trade Center on 9/11. He finds a complicated story of a man traumatized by alcohol, the Vietnam War and the fires of New York. Sometimes a hero can come from some of the most awful places imaginable. 
Q&A with director Steve McCarthy and producers Nancy Erika Smith and Neil Marc Mullin follows the screening.

Goes with the Open Book / Open Mind program with Tayari Jones about "Kin" the following week on Tuesday, September 15! Tickets cost $35 and include a signed copy of the book. (If for any reason you can't afford a ticket, come talk to me.)

We'll talk about Jones's conversation as well as "Kin," a poignant historical novel set in the civil rights era about two motherless childhood friends who take very different journeys: one to the storied HBCU Spellman College, the other to make her way in the world. 

TAYARI JONES is the author of four others novels, most recently the New York Times bestseller "An American Marriage," which was an Oprah’s Book Club selection and also appeared on Barack Obama’s summer reading list and his year-end roundup. It won the Women’s Prize for Fiction, the Aspen Words Literary Prize, and an NAACP Image Award and has been published in two dozen countries. Jones is the C.H. Candler Professor of English and Creative Writing at Emory University and lives in Atlanta.

title: Flames & Facts
description:
As part of Campus Fire Safety Awareness Month this September, we are planning a large-scale educational event focused on raising awareness about fire safety within the campus community. The highlight of the event will be a live burn demonstration using the National Fire Sprinkler Association's (NFSA) Side-by-Side Trailer. This will feature two mock dorm rooms—one with a sprinkler system and one without—to showcase the dramatic impact fire safety systems can have during a fire.The goal of the event is to educate students about the importance of working smoke detectors, not blocking or tampering with sprinkler heads, and understanding that while sprinkler systems may cause water damage, they ultimately save lives.

title: 🚶Yanticaw Park Nutley
description:
Let's Walk!!
Meet along Park Drive in Nutley near the Orechio Sports Complex. We'll walk about 3.5 mile through scenic Yanticaw Park, up to Kingsland St. and back. The path is paved and mostly flat.

Please check the event page beforehand in case of any changes. Inclement weather will cancel the walk.

The Yanticaw Park is an Essex County-owned park in Nutley, New Jersey. It is located between Centre Street and Chestnut Street, extending west to Passaic Avenue.

Essex County began purchasing land in 1911 for creation of the park. Wetlands in the park were drained, and a dam was set up to form a lake. The park was completed in 1914. In 1962, the lake, containing a small island was drained and a channel was dug as a continuation of the natural third river from the south.

PLEASE ARRIVE 5 MINUTES **EARLY** SO WE CAN START TO WALK ON TIME

Disclaimer: If you join us for a walk/hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap. Walk/hike will be canceled in the event of extreme weather.

description:
The 9/11 National Day of Service and Remembrance is long standing tradition at Montclair State University that honors the lives lost and heroic acts of September 11, 2001. Our volunteers commemorate the day through meaningful service projects that foster unity, civic responsibility, leadership, and often inspire long-term community engagement.
Come join us for a day of giving back!
Volunteers will have the opportunity to choose from 20+ service sites, both on and off campus, and engage in community service projects such as:

🍎 Meal distribution and food pantry support
🌳 Park and neighborhood cleanups
🎨 Community revitalization
✨ Activities for youth, seniors, and adults with disabilities
🧼 Assembling hygiene and snack kits
 And much more!

Here’s what you can expect:

⏰ Registration at 8:00 - 8:30 AM. Event starts at 8:30 AM
🚌 Transportation provided to and from off-campus sites
🥯 Free breakfast and lunch to fuel your day
⏳ Service hours validation (for students/groups that need it)
👕 Exclusive 9/11 Day of Service T-Shirt
🧑‍🎓 Bloomfield College students will have a shuttle service provided
🎊 Icebreaker activities and giveaways!

 
IMPORTANT NOTE: You can only sign up for one service site due to each project running simultaneously. We will email you after registration if other information is needed for your site.

location: Grove Street Theatre, 130 Grove Street, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042, United States
description:
Apricot Sky Productions presents “Tributes,” two nights of new one-act plays and monologues by New Jerseyans, benefiting the National September 11 Memorial & Museum 
Twenty-five years after the attacks that reshaped this state, Apricot Sky Productions will stage Tributes, an evening of six short plays and three monologues, on Friday, September 11 and Saturday, September 12 at 8 p.m. at the Grove Street Theater. Admission is free. A $20 donation is suggested at the door, with all proceeds going to the National September 11 Memorial & Museum in New York City. 
The work is written by Livingston playwright Eric Alter and performed and directed entirely by New Jersey artists, many of whom watched that morning unfold from their own front steps. New Jersey lost roughly 700 residents on September 11, 2001. 
“I will never forget the loss of humanity we experienced firsthand,” Alter said. “We aren’t helpless. One thing we can do is help the survivors and the families.” 
Not every piece is set on that day. “I didn’t want to hit the audience over the head,” Alter said. “The goal is to balance the weight with some levity.” 
The lineup ranges from The Eleventh of September, in which a man is pulled in two directions until he must make a defining choice, to Spin Doctor Love, a comedy about an aging DJ being pushed out of the booth, to And Now I Read to You, about a woman facing memory loss and the former student who returns to remind her what she meant to him. 
The Grove Street Theater seats 360, is wheelchair accessible, and offers free parking. Reservations are encouraged at (973) 509-2350. Seating is general admission. Donations accepted in cash, Venmo, or Zelle only. No credit or debit cards. Recommended for ages 12 and up.

title: 9/11 day of Service: Campus Blitz
description:
Honor the spirit of service on Montclair State University's Annual 9/11 Day of Service by helping ensure every eligible Red Hawk has the opportunity to make their voice heard.
Join the Office of Civic and Voter Engagement for Race to the Ballot: Campus Takeover, a campus-wide service initiative that empowers students to become civic ambassadors. During this hands-on volunteer experience, you'll learn how to confidently engage your peers in nonpartisan conversations about voting, assist them with the voter registration process, and encourage them to make a pledge to show up on Election Day.
No previous experience or political knowledge is required—just a willingness to serve your campus community and help others participate in our democracy. Our team will provide all the training, resources, and support you need to feel comfortable talking with fellow students and answering common questions about voter registration and upcoming elections.
As New Jersey's voter registration deadline approaches, volunteers will work alongside Civic and Voter Engagement staff to reach students across campus through pop-up voter registration stations and outreach efforts. Together, we'll help ensure every student has access to accurate, trusted, and nonpartisan election information.
As a volunteer, you will learn how to:

Assist students with registering to vote or updating their voter registration
Encourage fellow students to pledge to vote on Election Day
Answer common questions about voter registration and voting options
Connect students with trusted, nonpartisan election resources
Engage in respectful, nonpartisan conversations about civic participation
Help create a campus culture that values democratic engagement

By participating, you'll gain valuable leadership, communication, and outreach skills while making a meaningful impact on campus. Every conversation has the potential to inspire someone to participate in our democracy, and every new voter strengthens our community.
Whether you're passionate about civic engagement or simply looking for a meaningful way to give back on the 9/11 Day of Service, this is an opportunity to serve your fellow students while helping build a more informed, engaged, and connected campus.
No experience is necessary—just bring your enthusiasm, a willingness to make a difference, and a commitment to serving others. Together, we'll help every Red Hawk get election ready, one conversation at a time.

description:
LEGO Robotics for Elementary Kids (Grades K–5) 
LEGO Robotics at Kinetic Minds introduces kids to engineering and beginner coding through hands-on building, testing, and problem-solving using LEGO robotics kits. 
In this small-group, drop-in friendly workshop, kids work in pairs to build real robots, program simple behaviors, and improve their designs through guided challenges. The focus is on curiosity, experimentation, and learning how things work—there’s no single “right” build and no step-by-step cookie-cutter instructions. 
Workshops are intentionally capped at a low student-to-instructor ratio to support collaboration, confidence, and meaningful learning. 
Kids will explore:
• Engineering and building with LEGO robotics components
• Beginner coding concepts (motors, sensors, cause and effect)
• Testing, debugging, and iterating designs
• Teamwork, communication, and explaining ideas 
Details:
• 60-minute session
• Small-group format
• No prior experience required 
Community Sponsorship:
20% of seats are reserved for community sponsorship. Families interested in sponsored spots can email info@kineticmindscreative.com
for details.

description:

title: North Pocono Happy Hike
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us on this point-to-point hike, tracing historic Rail lines and other interesting and random stuff through the Northern tier of the Pocono Mountains.
We meet on the Old State Road at the trailhead for the North Pocono Rail Trail.
From here, we will head West and shuttle with his few cars as possible to our start.
from there, we will meander along some abandoned railroad beds, as well as some old turnpike routes, with only very short bits of road between.
There may be one bridge on the way those with height issues won't like.
Aside from that, the route is almost entirely clear and easy. Some might have uneven service, and only about 3 mi is improved surface.
Everyone should come prepared with everything they need because we are only passing by one location where we can refill on any food or drink.Distance is about 15 mi.
If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374

title: SMC Trail Work Volunteer Day
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
**TRAIL WORK will continue rerouting the Hogenauer Trail** (we are making progress!) up the slope and away from recently installed property fences. **Meet At:** Dog Park/ Wildflower Preserve, 11 Bear Lane, Maplewood. From there, we will walk to Crater View on Crest drive and then to the Hogenauer trail work site. (Note: While we normally meet the first Sudnay of each month, this volunteer day was shifted after the Labor Day weekend.)

Trail work is physically challenging but very satisfying as we use hand tools to build and repair trails. Participants must be 15+ years. Those younger than 18 must be accompanied by an adult. Participants **should wear long pants** due to [ticks](https://www.somocon.org/?page_id=193928&fb) and thron bushes and sturdy shoes, and bring gloves (though backup gloves will be available). Tools, water, and a snack will be provided. (Registration is not required though if you sign up on Meetup, it helps us know how many tools to bring.) Only heavy, steady rain cancels.

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Sundays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.

⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.

🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).

**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**🧯DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.
source: Meetup: NJ Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More

title: Concert: Marc Berger
description:
Presentation

RIDE currently offers ten cinematic recordings that capture the grandeur and allure of the West while examining its profound origins in the American psyche. Marc and Mike Ricciardi created the album, which is based on Marc's lifelong love affair with the American West. "Twister" has a melancholy message and beat, "Take It on the Chin" is about taming a wild horse, "Time Waits For No Man" is about a sexy, mind-blowing encounter in the middle of nowhere, and seven more scenic stops make up RIDE's Great American Frontier tour.

 

About the artist

Marc's life revolves around two passions: composing and performing original songs and touring the American West. At SXSW Music Festival and Kerrville Folk Festival, he has opened for big stars like Bob Dylan and sang his antinuclear hymn "The Last One," a mainstay of Richie Havens' shows.

The program features Chinese instruments such as the erhu, pipa, guzheng, and ruan, alongside Japanese taiko and shinobue, African percussion, jazz piano, lute, guitar, cello, double bass, voice, and more. 
 
The Montclair performance will take place on Sunday, September 13, 2026, at 3:00 p.m. in Memorial Auditorium at Montclair State University. The event is co-sponsored by the Department of Global Cultural Studies.

title: 60th Anniversary of MLK in Montclair - 'King in the Wilderness' Film Screening and Discussion
location: Montclair Main - Auditorium, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a free Adult School program. Please register below.

The Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr, visited Montclair High School on Sept. 11, 1966 to speak at the retirement of Rev. D.C. Rice, pastor of Union Baptist Church and an early mentor. A planned ceremony at Montclair High school was met with community uproar, leading to two separate King speeches on school grounds.

We will recognize the 60th anniversary of this event with a film screening of King in the Wilderness (2018) by a discussion and Q&A moderated by Dr. Leslie Wilson of Montclair State University.

"King in the Wilderness offers a window into the final years of the civil rights icon's life after the signing of the Voting Right Acts of 1965 and amid an American landscape divided by the Vietnam War and tensions over race and poverty. King's unwavering commitment to nonviolence and compassion shines through in archived footage and the stories of those who were around him."

title: The Assembly of Lovers - Sufi Drum Circle
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Community drum and chant circle rooted in Sufi prayer. 
Meets every other Monday:  September 14, September 28, etc. 
Contribution: Sliding scale donation $20–$40 (no one will be turned away) 
This is a vibrant Community Drum and Chanting Circle, where we drum and chant from our hearts into the universe. This experience is open to absolutely everyone, regardless of background or belief system—all that’s required is an open heart and a willingness to connect through sound.  The term ‘lover’ in this context refers to seekers on the Sufi path who are longing for union with the divine energy.  You can think of this gathering as an expansion of the sema sufi meditations we used to offer.  It is looser in form, more focused on music, and does not necessarily involve whirling, although it is welcome if you are called to it. 
There is a rhythm older than thought. A pulse that moves beneath language, beneath belief, beneath the self that thinks it’s separate. The Mystics knew this. The Sufis practiced it in Majalis al-‘Ushshāq. The Assembly of Lovers. Not lovers of ideas. Not lovers of comfort. Lovers magnetized by the Beloved. Those who’ve tasted the Divine Honey and cannot forget. Whose hearts remember what the mind has been taught to ignore. This is a gathering for those who feel the pull. The Assembly of Lovers meets twice each month, a rhythm of remembrance. Each gathering deepens the last. The circle becomes a living pulse of devotion. If you have a drum, bring it. Medicine drums, frame drums, and ceremony drums are all welcome. The circle grows stronger when every heartbeat joins the rhythm. 
The Flow 
Opening (5 minutes)
We set intention. A short prayer to open the way. To align the heart toward what is Real. 
Chanting and Rhythm (30-40 minutes)
Using the Sufi Chants of the Heart as a guide (our vision is for the chants to grow to what the individuals in the circle are inspired to invoke), we share simple chants. The drum holds the pulse. The voice follows. The meanings are offered, not explained. 
Repetition is the technology. The heart softens through return. Through invoking the Divine until the one invoking dissolves. 
Silent Resting (5-10 minutes)
After the chanting, we sit. No guidance. No instruction. 
The echo of the words and rhythms settles. The heart rests in what was touched. 
Closing (5 minutes)
A prayer of Unity. Of Oneness. We complete the circle and return to silence. 
Gratitude for what was offered. For what was received. 
  
Who This Is For 
This is for those who’ve felt the pull and don’t know what to call it. 
For those tired of spiritual talk that never touches the ground. 
For those who suspect that the heart knows a language the mind cannot translate. 
For those who long. 
Not for something. Not for someone. 
Just longing itself. The flame that keeps you moving toward what you cannot name but cannot forget. 
Osama Janakat 
 
Osama studied Mathematics and Physics at Rutgers University, laying a foundation of analytical thinking that complements his creative pursuits. As a beat-maker and music producer, he explores the intriguing connections between music, philosophy, and spirituality. 
Born in Jordan with Circassian roots, Osama’s move to the US in 2004 sparked a journey of inner exploration and spiritual discovery. An avid student of the Sufi tradition, he continues to seek wisdom that bridges cultures and disciplines, finding harmony in the interplay of art and spirituality.

title: (Montclair Campus) National Voter Registration Day: Race to the Ballot
description:
Join thousands of colleges, universities, nonprofits, businesses, and community organizations across the country as we celebrate National Voter Registration Day—the nation's largest single-day voter registration effort. This annual, nonpartisan initiative brings Americans together with one shared goal: helping eligible voters get registered, informed, and prepared to participate in our democracy.
Join us on September 17 from 12:00–4:00 PM in the Student Center Ballrooms and on the Quad as Montclair State University celebrates this national movement with an afternoon of civic engagement, entertainment, and community.
This year's event is proudly presented in collaboration with the Office of Commuter Life as part of Commuter Life Appreciation Week (CLAW). Together, we're celebrating the important role commuter students play in our campus community while encouraging every Red Hawk to become an informed and engaged participant in our democracy.
Whether you're registering to vote for the first time, updating your voter registration, or learning more about the upcoming election, Race to the Ballot is your one-stop destination to get election ready.
The event will kick off with welcoming remarks from Montclair State University President Dr. Jonathan Koppell, who will officially open the celebration by speaking about the importance of civic participation and the power of student voices. Throughout the afternoon, you'll also hear from special guest speakers who will share their perspectives on the importance of voting, civic leadership, and making a difference in our communities.
Enjoy a fun-filled afternoon featuring:

A giant patriotic inflatable obstacle course
Yard games and interactive activities
Free food served throughout the event
Music, giveaways, and civic swag
Voter registration assistance and nonpartisan election resources
Interactive activities hosted by campus and community partners

Be sure to stay for the entire event! Students who remain through the closing program will be entered into a raffle for a chance to win an exciting grand prize.
Together, we're joining a nationwide effort that has helped millions of Americans prepare to vote. Race to the Ballot is more than a voter registration event—it's a celebration of civic participation, community, and the belief that every voice has the power to shape the future.
The race starts here. The finish line is the ballot box. Register, get informed, and join the movement!













Hosted by: Campus Activities, Civic & Voter Engagement, Office of Commuter Life

Additional Information can be found at: https://montclair.campuslabs.com/engage/event/12539370

title: Sales-Driven Metrics: Know What Counts
location: Online – Virtual, Montclair, NJ, 07042, United States
description:
Know what to track, ditch what doesn’t matter, and finally trust your marketing numbers.
Drowning in dashboards but still not sure if your marketing is actually working? Sounds familiar. Most small business owners are tracking numbers that feel good but don’t mean much—while the metrics that actually drive growth go unnoticed. In this virtual Power Hour, we’ll cut through the noise and get clear on:
– Where to focus — which platforms actually deserve your time and attention (and which ones you can safely ignore)
– Vanity metrics unmasked — the likes, followers, and impressions that look impressive but rarely move the needle
– What really matters — the handful of metrics that tell you whether your marketing is generating real business results
Walk away with a simple framework for reading your marketing data with confidence, so you can stop guessing and start making decisions that actually grow your business.
Perfect for small business owners who want less noise and more clarity in their marketing.

title: Tuesday Night Figure Drawing - Open Studio
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Tuesday Night Figure Drawing – Open Studio 
*Cover art by Ling Chen. 











Tuesday night at The Space is your invitation to drop in, find your creative flow, and practice your drawing skills. 
Each week a different nude model serves as our muse as we pursue creative expression through observation and mark making. We challenge how we see and what we want to say — observing the nuances of the human form, its moods, character, and light — and do our best to capture something in the moment that tells a story. 
This has become a tight-knit, supportive community of seekers — artists, experimenters, and curious souls drawn together by the shared pursuit of capturing the living human form. Use the time to refine your skills, experiment with different media, and deepen your understanding of anatomy, gesture, and proportion. Challenge your process if you have one, or begin to develop one if you don’t. Learn to truly see. 
Each session features a variety of poses, from quick gesture sketches to longer, more detailed studies. Whether you’re looking to sharpen your technical abilities, loosen up your line work, or simply enjoy the meditative experience of drawing from life, this open studio is designed to support individual growth in a collaborative atmosphere. All skill levels are welcome – we’ve even had poets drop in and compose verses to the vibe in the room. 
Bring your preferred supplies — charcoal, graphite, ink, pastels, and paint are all welcome. Basic drawing materials are available if you don’t have any, and the shop has drawing pads and supplies for sale. No formal instruction is provided, but peer feedback and self-guided exploration are always part of the mix. 
Good music. Good people. See you Tuesday. 7 – 9:30 pm at the Space. 
Tickets are set at a capacity of 12, but we accommodate up to 18 for those paying in cash. 











“The object isn’t to make art, its to be in that wonderful state which makes art inevitable.” – Robert Henri

title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes)
description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

title: Understanding Medicare
description:
Confused about Medicare? Join us for an informative session that breaks down the basics of this federal health insurance program. Learn who qualifies, including adults age 65 and older, younger individuals with disabilities, and those with End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD).

We’ll explain the different parts of Medicare—Part A (hospital insurance), Part B (medical insurance), and Part D (prescription drug coverage)—and what services each covers. The program will also explore your coverage options, including Original Medicare with supplemental (Medigap) plans and Medicare Advantage (Part C).

This session is ideal for anyone approaching Medicare eligibility, caregivers, or those looking to better understand their health coverage choices.

Presented by Medicare Specialist Jacki Spear.

title: (Bloomfield Campus) National Voter Registration Day: Race to the Ballot
location: Deacon's Den and Talbott Hall Quad
description:
Join thousands of colleges, universities, nonprofits, businesses, and community organizations across the country as we celebrate National Voter Registration Day—the nation's largest single-day voter registration effort. This annual, nonpartisan initiative brings Americans together with one shared goal: helping eligible voters get registered, informed, and prepared to participate in our democracy.
Join us on September 17 from 12:00–4:00 PM in the Student Center Ballrooms and Quad as Montclair State University celebrates this national movement with an afternoon of civic engagement, entertainment, and community.
This year's event is proudly presented in collaboration with the Office of Commuter Life as part of Commuter Life Appreciation Week (CLAW). Together, we're celebrating the important role commuter students play in our campus community while encouraging every Red Hawk to become an informed and engaged participant in our democracy.
Whether you're registering to vote for the first time, updating your voter registration, or learning more about the upcoming election, Race to the Ballot is your one-stop destination to get election ready.
The event will kick off with welcoming remarks from Montclair State University President Dr. Jonathan Koppell, who will officially open the celebration by speaking about the importance of civic participation and the power of student voices. Throughout the afternoon, you'll also hear from special guest speakers who will share their perspectives on the importance of voting, civic leadership, and making a difference in our communities.
Enjoy a fun-filled afternoon featuring:

A giant patriotic inflatable obstacle course
Yard games and interactive activities
Free food served throughout the event
Music, giveaways, and civic swag
Voter registration assistance and nonpartisan election resources
Interactive activities hosted by campus and community partners

Be sure to stay for the entire event! Students who remain through the closing program will be entered into a raffle for a chance to win an exciting grand prize.
Together, we're joining a nationwide effort that has helped millions of Americans prepare to vote. Race to the Ballot is more than a voter registration event—it's a celebration of civic participation, community, and the belief that every voice has the power to shape the future.
The race starts here. The finish line is the ballot box. Register, get informed, and join the movement!

Hosted by: Civic & Voter Engagement, Campus Activities at Bloomfield, Office of Commuter Life

Additional Information can be found at: https://montclair.campuslabs.com/engage/event/12539388

title: Jean Luc Godard's Breathless (1960): Introduction to French Film
description:
Program

We invite you to join us for this fascinating introduction to the French New Wave, which redefined storytelling in film during the '50s and '60s. The event commences with a perceptive introduction given by Gerard Amsellem, who is an artist, educator, and founder of New Wave Productions and the Institute of Art and Film Studies. It concludes with a showing of Breathless (À bout de souffle), a legendary film by Jean-Luc Godard, which is widely regarded as the film that sparked modern cinema. Stay for an interactive Q&A with Amsellem after the film to discuss the film's unique cutting techniques, the groundbreaking roles played by the performers, and the director's vision.

Artist

Gerard Amsellem is an artist, educator, and filmmaker holding dual citizenship in the U.S. and France. With a background in painting and advanced degrees in French literature and art history from the University of Paris, he later continued his education at New York University's Tisch School of the Arts. Amsellem has directed several short films, including "Bartleby" (2013), which received a Director’s Citation from the Black Maria Film Festival and was an Official Selection at various festivals. His production company, New Waves Productions, focuses on promoting film as an art form and ensuring public access to quality cinema.

title: Zoom: Successfully Navigating College Admissions
description:
Register HERE





We are offering this Zoom presentation to help families of high school juniors, sophomores, and freshmen better understand the college admissions process and how to successfully navigate today’s changing landscape.

 

The session will cover current college admissions trends and strategies, the evolving test optional environment, the importance of researching and visiting colleges to find the right fit, and key timelines and action steps that can make this fall productive while easing stress around the college admissions process.

 

We will also take a close look at the holistic admissions review process, including what admissions officers value when evaluating applicants and how students can develop a strong personal narrative that reflects their strengths, interests, character, and experiences.

 

Another focus will be on the role of community service and the growing importance of meaningful “passion projects.” We will discuss how students can turn their interests, values, and experiences into authentic activities that foster personal growth, demonstrate character, and show positive impact. Admissions officers place great emphasis on character, and thoughtful service can help students show initiative, empathy, and a genuine commitment to helping their communities.

 

This program is recommended for parents and their high school teens. It provides a clear and strategic overview of what students should prioritize this fall for a successful college admissions journey and how to approach the process with confidence and less stress.

 

The presentation will be led by Ron Feuchs and Jackie Tepper, partners at Stand Out For College, LLC (www.standoutforcollege.com).

title: Book Talk: A Good Man by Debbie Slevin
location: Montclair Main - Classroom, Montclair Public Library
description:
Slevin delivers a riveting novel about two abused women in New York City in the wake of the 9/11 attacks… A moving novel about tragedy and recovery. -- Kirkus Reviews

Join author Debbie Slevin for a Book Talk. Her debut novel, A Good Man, explores friendship, domestic abuse, heroism, resilience, and the complicated nature of goodness in the aftermath of September 11. Her work begins with a question that refuses to let go. In journalism, nonfiction, theater, and fiction, Debbie explores the extraordinary moments hidden inside ordinary lives.

www.debbieslevin.com



Reviews
“… A powerful story with unforgettable characters, filled with compassion, humor, and hard truths…the healing power of friendship…” Alice M. Greenwald, Former President & CEO,
National September 11 Memorial & Museum.

"Debbie Slevin is a writer of extraordinary grace, wit, and feeling… inventive, daring, and brilliant on the nuances of the human heart." Hilary Leichter, author of “Terrace Story,” and "Temporary", winner of 2026 Whiting Award in Fiction.

As the story opens in 2001, journalist Elizabeth Allen drags herself up off the floor after her husband, a disgraced rock star, has brutally beaten her in their Upper West Side apartment before leaving. Across the city, Fancy Maguire showers after being raped by her fireman spouse. The 9/11 attack brings these women together after Fancy’s husband dies as a first responder at the Twin Towers and Elizabeth decides to rehabilitate her own fading career by writing about the experience of survivors. Although the two women’s circumstances are different in many ways, they find common ground in their shared despair at the hands of supposedly “good” men: “Was Frank a good man?” muses Elizabeth. “For all public accounts of his life, he was. Only Fancy and I knew the truth.” Both women struggle with their knowledge of their husbands’ violent natures. At the same time, Elizabeth and Fancy both mourn the men they once loved and think carefully about how they want the unsuspecting world to think of their spouses. Slevin structures the story around Elizabeth’s first-person narration, interspersing transcripts of her interviews with Fancy and members of her extended family and friends. Although Fancy’s experience of domestic abuse ends with her husband’s death, Slevin effectively maintains the narrative momentum with the ongoing story of Elizabeth’s traumatic marriage, which continues for a year after the attacks. Her arc notably mirrors the city’s own journey from despair to hope as she suffers a final, brutal attack, recovers, and experiences a new life as part of a larger community, including Fancy and her family. A
moving novel about tragedy and recovery. -- Kirkus Reviews

title: Tea & Tarot - A Bookclub Style Discussion Group
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Monthly Gathering | Thursday, September 17th | 7:00 PM – 8:30 PM | The Space | $25 
Calling all tarot lovers, both new and seasoned!  Join us for an intimate way of exploring the cards. 
What could be better than a cozy evening of warm tea and deep conversation? Join us for Tea & Tarot with Gina Devine—a monthly, book club-style discussion group created to deepen our connection with the archetypes of the tarot through community and shared insight. 
Rather than a formal class, this is a casual meet-up where we treat the tarot as a living text. Based on the psychological insights of Carl Jung, we will explore the Major Arcana not just as fortune-telling tools, but as mirrors of our own lives, rituals, and transformations. 
The Experience 
Each month, we open a new gateway of creative and spiritual exploration. Our time together includes: 

Archetypal Deep Dives: We’ll focus on a specific theme or set of cards each session, discussing their symbolism and how they show up in our modern world.
Collaborative Readings: A chance to pull cards for one another in a supportive, low-pressure environment.
Ritual & Connection: We’ll sip tea, share stories, and find common ground in the mysteries of the deck.
Intuitive Growth: Whether you’ve been reading for decades or just bought your first deck, you’ll leave with a deeper understanding of the “BodyGraph” of the tarot.

What to Bring 
To make the most of our evening, please bring the following if you can: 

Your Tarot Deck: Any deck you feel connected to.  If you don’t have any we have some available here to use.

A Notebook: For capturing insights, spreads, and “aha” moments.

Investment: $25 
Stay Connected: Sign up for the Soul Centric Tarot Newsletter here.

Your Guide Gina Devine
Instagram: @gina.devine 

Gina Devine is an esoteric artist, intuitive tarot reader, writer, educator and guide. 
She has provided thousands of readings for people all over the world, and leads both protection and tarot workshops. Her approach to guidance is loving, grounded and human. Although she also teaches traditional tarot classes, her tea and tarot discussion group was birthed from the knowing that people are more inclined to to be in tune with the archetypes of the cards and the messages they bring when they are allowed space to enjoy the tarot in a more casual setting – instead of forcefully trying to memorize them. The same way we find joy in discussing a book in community, the cards also call for us to convene together around them. Her approach is philosophical, therapeutic and creative, and she is on a mission to guide people toward unearthing a more intimate and honest relationship with their inner knowing through the art of divination. title: A.I.M by Kyle Abraham: White Space
description:
Run Time: 1 hour 
White Space brings together acclaimed composers, Jason Moran and Nico Muhly, for a haunting new collaborative score that pierces the heart of choreographer Kyle Abraham’s newest evening-length dance. At just over one hour, this dance work grounds its cast of 11 captivating dancers in a restless and thought-provoking world fueled by a vast movement vocabulary consisting of Abraham’s signature blend of classical and contemporary dance with a hip-hop underbelly. The score is performed live by two pianists on one piano, with echoes of pre-recorded hip-hop driving the collision of reality and idealism. 
“lush movement, infectious music and magnetic dancers…” (The New York Times) 
 
About A.I.M by Kyle Abraham: Celebrating its 20th anniversary throughout 2026, A.I.M by Kyle Abraham has been at the forefront of contemporary dance for nearly two decades and has become one of the most acclaimed touring companies in the world. A.I.M has been featured in Vogue, Essence, among many other publications, and was on the April 2025 cover of Harper’s Bazaar. The company is described as a “postmodern gumbo” with an ardent voice and artistic process informed by robust conversations with people from diverse perspectives. A.I.M performs works by Abraham as well as new and existing works by choreographers who have influenced Abraham’s artistry. 
Founded in 2006 and based in New York City, A.I.M has spent two decades at the forefront of the field. It has earned recognition for its “lush movement, infectious music and magnetic dancers…” (The New York Times), becoming one of the most acclaimed touring ensembles in the world. Grounded in a commitment to reshaping how artists are supported, the company provides dancers with 52-week salaries and retirement benefits, alongside royalty payments in perpetuity for their role in the creation of new work. A.I.M continues to expand what a contemporary dance company can be and who gets to imagine themselves within it. In doing so, the organization challenges the entire arts ecosystem to create space where more people can thrive. 
For more information, to get involved, or to purchase your A.I.M merchandise, please visit http://aimbykyleabraham.org. 
Follow A.I.M on Instagram @aimbykyleabraham and
Kyle Abraham on Instagram  @kyle_abraham_original_recipe

title: Bowling Night - North Jersey
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
This is an event for casual bowling at Montvale Lanes, 14 W. Grand Ave. All are welcome for **two games, food and drinks**, and any post- or pre-game hang out. Show up anytime! Questions or comments? You can message Andy Milone on Meetup, or call/text him at **201-234-9609**.

\*\*\* Before bowling, we might stop by the Pizza Parlour, 6 S. Kinderkamack Road in Montvale, for a few slices. Post a comment on the event page to gauge interest. **After bowling, we'll definitely be heading to The Ridge Diner, 125 Kinderkamack Road in Park Ridge, at 10:15 p.m. for some food and/or drinks.** \*\*\*

About the group: People of all ages, backgrounds and abilities are welcome! We're not professionals and we're not in a league. In fact, we're a group of people who probably each won't score more than 100 points and will land more than our fair share of gutter balls. There's no pressure at all!!!! We're not here to analyze your form or technique.

More event details: You pay for your own games, food and drinks. Please bring cash. The alley does not accept card. But there is an ATM on site. **The** **cost per player is $18 for two games** **and bowling shoes.** If you have your own shoes, the cost is $12. Please try to bring exact change since Andy will have a limited amount of cash. If you bring a $20 bill and he doesn't have change, any remainder would just go toward the bowling alley tip.

Food and drinks (alcoholic and non-alcoholic) are available on site, plus tables and an alley bar to hang at during the event. There is a dart board and a few arcade games, as well.

**What do you do when you get there?** Find the group inside around the front desk. Look for a growing group of people! Call or text Andy Milone at 201-234-9609 if you can't find us. Once Andy secures the lanes, please pay him before getting your bowling shoes and heading to the lanes.

**Please know that it is possible we have to wait 20-40 minutes until lane(s) free up.** It's also possible that we may have to relocate or cancel that night if there's a long wait list upon arrival. Please keep that in mind if traveling from far away!

For those who don't have cars or are looking to avoid driving, the Montvale Train Station is only like a five-minute walk from the bowling alley and can be reached via the Pascack Valley Line. Last train leaves at 12:20 a.m. and heads toward Hoboken. (https://gmtma.org/wp-content/uploads/2011/11/rail_system_map.jpg)

Many thanks to Taylor, one of our group participants, for recommending Montvale Lanes! You can learn more at: www.montvalelanes.com.

Hope you'll join us for our 26th bowling event, or consider attending one of our volleyball, ping pong, skating or other activities -> www.meetup.com/north-jersey-bowling-soccer-volleyball

If interested in staying touch with group members or conversing about future events, feel free to inquire about our WhatsApp group chat.

title: Flow Into Form:  A Qi Gong and Expressive Art Experience
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Saturday September 19 | 1 – 3 pm, $40  
Breathe. Move. Create. 
Facilitated by Niraj Shah – long-time qi-gong teacher and practitioner, and Naz Botas – artist and owner of the Space. 
If you’ve been craving a gentle reset—something grounding, nourishing, and expressive—this workshop is your invitation. 
In this two-hour workshop, you’ll move through repeating cycles of Qi Gong and intuitive art-making designed to calm your nervous system, soften tension in the body, and open your creative heart. 
You’ll experience: 

Qi Gong: slow, mindful movements paired with gentle breathwork to flow your energy and bring you into the present moment
Intuitive Art: using charcoal, ink, or pastels, you’ll make marks on wall-length paper as your body moves — both naturally and through guided Qi Gong sequences — allowing your inner experience to express itself visually

Across the session, we’ll repeat several short rounds of movement followed by mark-making, gradually building comfort, curiosity, and expression. By the end, you’ll be able to look at your paper and literally see the journey your body and breath took you on. 
No prior experience in art or Qi Gong is needed. Just a willingness to breathe, move, and let the paper receive whatever wants to come through. 
Expect a peaceful, meditative atmosphere.
A safe space.
And a sense of release you’ll carry with you long after the workshop ends. 
These practices help you: 

Let go of stress stored in the body
Feel more present and grounded
Reconnect with your authentic creativity
Express yourself without pressure or judgment

A beautiful experience for anyone seeking clarity, calm, and creative freedom! 
What to Bring: 

comfortable clothing you can move in
a water bottle
an open heart and curious mind

title: Buena Vista Social Club: The musical
description:
Learn about the fascinating history of the Buena Vista Social Club -- the band and the musical -- in this lecture by Rick Feingold.

Program

Before the revolution altered the course of Cuban music, a band of young musicians in Havana in the 1950s had already begun to shake things up. In a surprising twist, the band reunited forty years later to record the songs they had left behind, and the result was the best-selling album in the history of world music. Years later, the band would become the subject of a Tony-winning Broadway musical. Feingold's presentation will focus on the musical and include clips from the 1999 documentary film Son Cubano, as well as discussion of life in Cuba in the 1950s before the revolution.

Presenter

Rick Feingold oversaw the Latin Jazz series at the Performing Arts Center at Penn State University. In addition to extensive travels throughout Cuba, Feingold teaches history at Bergen Community College. Mr. Feingold has a Bachelor of Arts in History from Rutgers University and an MBA from Penn State University.

title: NJ Code & Coffee - September meetup
description:
NJ Code & Coffee
Calling all New Jersey techies to the monthly **NJ Code and Coffee** tech community meetup at the EqualSpace ES550 Tech & Innovation campus!

Code and Coffee is an inclusive, informal networking/co-working session for those in tech (and the tech-curious).
That includes operators, founders, and investors. Developers, data engineers, UX/UI designers, data scientists, product managers, software engineers, solution architects... **all are welcome!**

People of all skill and experience levels can attend, we love it that way. Many people (optionally) bring projects to work on, and many other people (optionally) socialize the entire time. It's entirely up to you!

Come grab a cup of coffee and meet new people, share stories, find collaborators, talk about everything tech, talk about everything NOT tech, take a break from job applications, get away from the computer screen, make connections, make conversation, **make friends!**

**Agenda:**
**2pm:** Doors open, networking starts
**2:30pm:** Intro circle
**3pm:** networking continues
**5pm:** event ends

**The Intro Circle**
**Near the beginning of the event (about 2:30 pm), we will do a standup in a circle:**
We first talk about organizer announcements, updates, and logistics. Then we go around the circle where each person says:

\*your name and job title/ role in tech/ tech stack,

* What you can help others with,
\*What you would like help with,
* Job opportunities you're hiring for OR announce that you are looking for one. If none, that's cool.

After the introduction circle, everything is self-organized.

title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**
**GPS:** 40.739791, -74.289181

title: Schuylkill River Special Hike
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us for this very interesting point to point hike in our Schuylkill River series! Distance will be about 15 miles and feature the Schuylkill River Trail, but also a lot of very interesting other things....
After meeting at the Schuylkill River Trail/Bartrum Trailhead on Market Street next to the Dry Wall place in Auburn PA, we will shuttle with as few vehicles as possible to the beginning.
The hike will begin covering the trail system at Kaercher Creek Park, which we've never visited before.
We'll weave around on most of their entire trail system, and then make our way through ball fields, and into downtown Hamburg.
We'll get on the Schuylkill River Trail here and mostly follow it back to Auburn area, but with some surprise side trips along the way.
One of the side trips will include locks and towpath on the Schuylkill Navigation that will be an out and back.
Most of the route will be pretty easy. The first bit will have a little bit of foot path, and one of the side trips may have some weeds, but nothing too terrible.
If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374

**🧯DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Long Pose Figure Drawing and Painting 
Cover art by Jake Yeh 
Sunday, September 20, 1 – 5 pm, $10 per hour or $35 for the full session 
“The object isn’t to make art, it’s to be in that wonderful state which makes art inevitable.” – Robert Henri 
This special Sunday session is an extended version of our beloved Tuesday night figure drawing, giving you a full four hours to sink deep into the work. Bring your favorite materials, settle in, listen to some good tunes in great company, and get into your flow.  This will be a great opportunity to create a more finished work of art, hone your portraiture skills, or work with a material that you don’t normally get to use. 
Our model will be dressed in character (more details coming soon) and serve as our muse for the afternoon.  Whether you want to loosen up your line work, push into a sustained study, or simply spend a slow Sunday afternoon drawing from life, this is your space to do it. 
You can stay for the full session, or drop in and pay by the hour for an hour or two. 
All skill levels welcome, from seasoned studio artists to total beginners. Even poets have been known to drop in. 
Materials such as charcoal, graphite, ink, pastels, and paints are all welcome. Basic drawing supplies available upon request. No formal instruction is given so it is a self-guided session. 
Check out our regular weekly Tuesday night sessions here.

title: Wildflower Sculpture Park Opening Reception
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
The [Wildflower Sculpture Park](https://www.somocon.org/visit/wildflower-sculpture-park/?mc_cid=887616f7ab&mc_eid=UNIQID) invites you to the opening of this year’s project, **Root System**, a collaborative, site-responsive exploration of roots, rhizomes, and interconnected systems of life.

Curatorial and artist talk will begin at 3:30pm. Light refreshments will be served.

Artists were encouraged to consider how ecological networks within the South Mountain Reservation connect to community, history, and ancestry, and to propose work that engages themes of resilience, symbiosis, and environmental stewardship.

PLEASE NOTE: You must sign up for EACH INDIVIDUAL SESSION. Signing up for one session does not register you for any following classes.

description:
Learn where and how to search for books, articles, and more. We’ll break down the differences between primary and secondary sources. We'll discuss "credible sources," both those from scholarly (peer-reviewed) journals and those from other sources. We'll also discuss, among other things, the differences between our two largest family of databases -- ProQuest and EBSCO. We want you to advance your searching skills so that you learn to have fun searching (a.k.a. researching). title: Mental Health Support Group (NAMI's Connection Recovery Peer Support Group)
description:
The Essex-Passaic Chapter of NAMI (The National Alliance on Mental Illness) Connection Recovery Peer Support Group Program meets on the 4th Tuesday of each month at the West Caldwell Library on 30 Clinton Road. 

NAMI is the most influential organization devoted to helping people with mental illness and their relatives and loved ones recover and deal with mental health issues. These meetings will be led by people having some form of mental illness. During these meetings, we will conduct peer support though all people interested in this organization are encouraged to attend. You do not have to sign up in advance. All meetings are kept confidential and are led by people specifically trained to conduct these meetings.

 NAMI Connection is a recovery peer support group program that offers respect, understanding, encouragement and hope. NAMI Connection groups are:

·       Free and confidential

·       Held monthly for 90 minutes  

·       Designed to connect, encourage, and support participants using a structured support group model

·       Led by trained facilitators living in recovery themselves

This meeting is for anyone ages 18  who is dealing with their own mental illness or a loved one's.

title: Tuesday Night Figure Drawing - Open Studio
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Tuesday Night Figure Drawing – Open Studio 
*Cover art by Ling Chen. 











Tuesday night at The Space is your invitation to drop in, find your creative flow, and practice your drawing skills. 
Each week a different nude model serves as our muse as we pursue creative expression through observation and mark making. We challenge how we see and what we want to say — observing the nuances of the human form, its moods, character, and light — and do our best to capture something in the moment that tells a story. 
This has become a tight-knit, supportive community of seekers — artists, experimenters, and curious souls drawn together by the shared pursuit of capturing the living human form. Use the time to refine your skills, experiment with different media, and deepen your understanding of anatomy, gesture, and proportion. Challenge your process if you have one, or begin to develop one if you don’t. Learn to truly see. 
Each session features a variety of poses, from quick gesture sketches to longer, more detailed studies. Whether you’re looking to sharpen your technical abilities, loosen up your line work, or simply enjoy the meditative experience of drawing from life, this open studio is designed to support individual growth in a collaborative atmosphere. All skill levels are welcome – we’ve even had poets drop in and compose verses to the vibe in the room. 
Bring your preferred supplies — charcoal, graphite, ink, pastels, and paint are all welcome. Basic drawing materials are available if you don’t have any, and the shop has drawing pads and supplies for sale. No formal instruction is provided, but peer feedback and self-guided exploration are always part of the mix. 
Good music. Good people. See you Tuesday. 7 – 9:30 pm at the Space. 
Tickets are set at a capacity of 12, but we accommodate up to 18 for those paying in cash. 











“The object isn’t to make art, its to be in that wonderful state which makes art inevitable.” – Robert Henri

title: Life Long Learning: Mary Cassatt: Impressionist Painter and Printmaker with Janet Mandel
location: JCC MetroWest | Maurice Levin Theater, 760 Northfield Ave, West Orange, NJ, 07052, United States
description:
In 2026, not only are we celebrating the 250th anniversary of the birth of the USA, but also the 100th anniversary of the death of artist Mary Cassatt. Janet Mandel will discuss how Cassatt, the only American among the Impressionists, has secured her place as a celebrated American icon. 
About the speaker: Janet Mandel retired after teaching for 32 years in the New Jersey public schools. She now presents illustrated lectures on art history at museums, adult schools, libraries, and senior centers. 
FREE for JCC Member; $15 Nonmember
 
Register Here
  
Sponsored by: 
 
  
DAY TRIP 
On Thursday, October 15, join us for a docent-led Impressionism and Beyond tour at the Philadelphia Museum of Art, featuring seven Mary Cassatt paintings. The trip will include admission to the Marcel Duchamp retrospective as well, a perfect complement to Janet’s March 2025 lecture.

title: 'The Shoes' Play Reading
description:
Come enjoy a reading of The Shoes before it hits the New York Winter Festival (NYWinterfest) this year!


The Shoes follows the story of Kent Warner, the man who changed the course of Hollywood history when he discovered Judy Garland's iconic ruby slippers from The Wizard of Oz hidden away in storage. Yet, behind the glitz and glamour of showbiz, Kent struggled with his identity, a sense of belonging, and the search for love—often using his passion for classic cinema to escape his own reality.

In a world of good and bad witches, of empty heads and aching hearts, Kent ultimately proved to be the courage at the center of it all.
